show: „Starzyński” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; autorska premiera musicalowa Teatru Syrena). VERIFIED FACTS about this production — the synopsis must not contradict any of them: (1) 🚨 The action takes place on the evening, night and morning of 26 and 27 OCTOBER 1939 — never 1941. These are Starzyński's last hours in Warsaw's city hall under German occupation. (2) Official facts: battered Warsaw, boundless helplessness, remorse, sadness and moral dilemmas; outside there are ruins, autumn, the approaching Zaduszki (All Souls') and darkness; ghosts crawl out of memories and dream mixes with waking. (3) Official cast: Stefan Starzyński, Stefania Witkowska/Syrena/Reklamiara, Adam Brodziński, Stanisław Lorentz, Władysław Studnicki, Matka, Ojciec/Józef Piłsudski, Józia, Sylwester Wojewódzki/Lech Niemojewski, Paulina/Ludwika Nitschowa, Żołnierz Gestapo. (4) The production uses fragments of Adam Mickiewicz's 'Dziady', quotations from Starzyński's own speeches, and Ludwika Nitschowa's words from Polish Radio reportage. It is inspired by Grzegorz Piątek's biography 'Starzyński. Prezydent z pomnika'.
synopsis:
Stefan Starzyński keeps vigil in his office at Warsaw’s ratusz as evening falls on 26 October 1939. A month after the city’s capitulation, he remains amid a wounded capital: beyond the windows lie rubble, autumn, deepening darkness and the imminence of Zaduszki, while the German occupation closes around him.

Through the night, the mayor’s workroom becomes a shifting inner landscape in which memory, nightmare and waking life can no longer be cleanly separated. Starzyński confronts the consequences of decisions made during the defence of Warsaw and the painful mismatch between public duty and private exhaustion. His helplessness, grief and remorse summon figures from his past and imagination: Matka and Ojciec/Józef Piłsudski; Józia; Paulina/Ludwika Nitschowa; Sylwester Wojewódzki/Lech Niemojewski; and the critic Władysław Studnicki. Stanisław Lorentz, nearby in the ratusz, anchors the night in the beleaguered city’s immediate reality.

Yet the boundaries of the office repeatedly give way. Stefania Witkowska appears not only as herself but as Syrena and Reklamiara, while Adam Brodziński becomes a troubling, spectral interlocutor. Voices from the city’s civic life, personal attachments and political disputes press upon Starzyński, forcing him to revisit ambitions, failures and responsibilities that cannot be repaired. As the approaching All Souls’ season lends the night the atmosphere of a modern-day Dziady, the dead and the remembered seem to crawl out of his consciousness. By dawn on 27 October, the presence of Żołnierz Gestapo turns the long vigil into the threshold of Starzyński’s arrest.

The musical strips the heroic monument of certainty and places a human being inside an unbearable historical moment. It asks how courage can coexist with doubt, whether responsibility ever ends, and what remains of a city’s conscience when its world has fallen into ruins.

show: 忍劇「NARUTO-ナルト-」(2027年2月〜 京都・南座;原作 岸本斉史;演出 植木豪;構成 亀田真二郎). VERIFIED FACTS about this production — the synopsis must not contradict any of them: (1) 🚨 This production is a NON-VERBAL ninja live show ('ノンバーバル忍者ライブショー'): no dialogue and no songs. It uses actors' action, acrobatics and aerial work fused with projection mapping and illusion, plus all the stage machinery of the kabuki theatre Minamiza. (2) 🚨 The only plot statement the producers make is that it depicts the story of the NARUTO boyhood arc (少年篇), in which Naruto Uzumaki grows up together with his companions in the Hidden Leaf Village. Do NOT retell specific manga arcs — no source says this show stages the Land of Waves, Zabuza and Haku, the Chūnin Exams, Mizuki, Iruka or the Scroll of Sealing. (3) Official characters announced: Naruto Uzumaki, Sasuke Uchiha, Sakura Haruno, Kakashi Hatake. Do not introduce others by name. (4) 🚨 Never write a sentence about what 'the official production identifies' or about sources, adaptations or versions. Describe only what happens. (5) It is acceptable for this synopsis to be shorter than usual, because very little plot detail has been published.
synopsis:
Naruto Uzumaki races through Konohagakure with the restless energy of a boy determined to prove himself. Around him, the village becomes a shifting world of training, rivalry, mischief and daring physical challenges, where a leap across open space, a sudden disappearance or a perfectly timed evasive move can say more than words.

Naruto’s path unfolds alongside Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno, whose sharply contrasting temperaments create a changing rhythm of competition, frustration, trust and shared effort. Each encounter tests how far the three can move as individuals and how much stronger they may become by responding to one another. Under Kakashi Hatake’s watchful guidance, their movements grow more disciplined, their instincts more closely connected, and their separate ambitions begin to form the beginnings of a team.

The action carries Naruto and his companions through a world where ninja techniques transform the space around them. Bodies vault, tumble and soar; shadows multiply; impossible escapes and sudden reversals turn danger into spectacle. Konohagakure itself seems to expand and contract with their struggles, becoming at once a familiar home, a training ground and a place where young ninja confront the distance between who they are and who they hope to become. As Naruto keeps pushing forward, setbacks become invitations to try again, and each act of courage draws his companions more deeply into the same journey.

At its heart, the story is about growth: the effort to find one’s strength while learning to stand beside others. It celebrates perseverance, friendship and the exhilaration of discovering that even the most unruly ambition can become a source of connection.

show: „A Charlie Brown Christmas: Live on Stage” (touring stage production adapted from Charles M. Schulz; music by Vince Guaraldi). VERIFIED FACTS about this production — the synopsis must not contradict any of them: (1) 🚨 Charlie Brown is asked to direct the NEIGHBORHOOD Christmas play — not a school play. The official touring copy says the Peanuts gang 'produce their own Christmas play and ultimately learn the true meaning of the season'. (2) 🚨 Linus's speech is the turning point of the work and must appear: when Charlie Brown asks whether anyone knows what Christmas is all about, Linus steps into the spotlight and answers. (3) Officially named characters: Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Lucy, Linus, and 'the whole Peanuts gang'. Lucy runs her own five-cent psychiatric booth — Charlie Brown pays her for advice; she does not set it up for him. (4) 🚨 Do NOT include Peppermint Patty: she first appeared in 1966, after the 1965 work this show adapts. Sally, Schroeder, Violet, Frieda and Patty are safer, but the official copy names only Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Lucy and Linus — keep other names to a minimum. (5) Other canonical beats: Snoopy decorates his doghouse for the lights-and-display contest; Charlie Brown chooses a small bare tree instead of a shiny aluminium one; the others mock it, then restore it together. Music by Vince Guaraldi.
synopsis:
Charlie Brown feels increasingly out of step with the holiday bustle around him. Hoping to understand why Christmas has left him so low, he visits Lucy’s five-cent psychiatric booth and pays for her advice; she decides that what he needs is responsibility and persuades him to direct the neighborhood Christmas play. While the whole Peanuts gang prepares to sing, dance, and rehearse, Charlie Brown tries to bring some order and sincerity to the production, but his directions are quickly drowned out by noise, playfulness, and everyone’s competing ideas about Christmas.

Elsewhere, Snoopy turns the season into a spectacle, covering his doghouse with decorations in hopes of winning the neighborhood lights-and-display contest. Charlie Brown is dismayed by this commercial frenzy and searches instead for something simple that might give the play the proper feeling. At the tree lot, surrounded by shiny aluminium trees, he chooses a small, bare living tree. Linus accompanies him back, but the others greet Charlie Brown’s choice with ridicule, seeing only a scraggly tree rather than the festive centerpiece they expected.

Hurt and bewildered, Charlie Brown finally asks whether anyone knows what Christmas is all about. Linus steps into the spotlight and answers by recounting the Nativity story, transforming Charlie Brown’s question into the play’s quiet emotional turning point. With that reminder, Charlie Brown resolves not to let appearances and commercialism define the season. Yet when he decorates the little tree with a single ornament, it bends beneath the weight, and he leaves in despair.

Linus and the rest of the gang return to the tree, recognize that it merely needs care, and restore it together with decorations. When Charlie Brown comes back, the once-mocked tree has become a joyful symbol of the Christmas they have rediscovered.

The musical contrasts noisy holiday display with generosity, faith, and friendship, carried by Vince Guaraldi’s music. Its final image affirms that Christmas gains meaning not from perfection or possessions, but from shared kindness and the willingness to see value in what others overlook.
